newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dow soars after jobs data gives rate comfort.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dow soars after jobs data gives rate comfort.

text.p: Wall Street soared and the dollar briefly hit a 39-month high on Friday after jobs reports in the United States and Germany showed the sharply divergent prospects of the two economic powerhouses.

The dollar leapt to a high of 1.7423 marks after key U.S. non-farm payrolls figures provided a mixed picture of the labour market. Although the currency later beat a sharp retreat on profit-taking, the Dow had soared 100 points by the time European markets closed as U.S. investors decided the jobs data did not give the Federal Reserve any reason to raise interest rates next month.

The U.S. jobless rate unexpectedly fell to 4.8 percent in May, its lowest level since October 1973 and in stark contrast to figures from the German Bundesbank. They showed 11.4 percent of Germans were out of work in May based on adjusted data, compared with 11.2 percent in April.
Even the German market jumped to a new trading high in bourse trade and responded positively in post-bourse trading to the strength of the dollar and U.S. data.
The rest of Europe's main bourses also had a good day, with London advancing 1.5 percent, despite the Bank of England raising bank base rates by a quarter point to 6.5 percent.
Bond markets wobbled but then steadied after the U.S. figures initially spooked traders by showing jobs growth slowed sharply in May although earlier months were revised upwards significantly.
Prices of the rare precious metals platinum and palladium remained at dizzy heights because of delays in Russian exports. Russia is the largest exporter of palladium.
Platinum fixed at $497.00 an ounce, its highest level since August 23, 1990 and palladium was valued at $240.00, its highest price since March 1980.

The German jobs figures, which showed a seasonally adjusted rise of 56,000 in the number of people out of work to 4.358 million, intensified concerns over how Bonn could cut its budget deficit to the 3.0 percent of GDP required for the European single currency.
The foreign exchange market responded by pushing the dollar higher, and investors piled into dollars after the U.S. report.

But traders grew wary of the speed of the mark's decline and the prospect of European central bank support to stabilise the situation. This prompted a wave of dollar profit-taking late in the session.
By 1615 GMT the dollar had slipped to 1.7261 marks, down from late Thursday's 1.7285. Against the yen it stood at 115.23 versus 115.65.

Despite gloomy comments from German officials at the prospects of a revival in the jobs market, the country's share market remained strong although the DAX index closed off its intraday record of 3,708.25 at 3,695.29, up 0.61 percent.
In later screen-based trade the IBIS-DAX index climbed back through 3,700 and ended at 3,700.53.
SGL Carbon, which closed bourse trade down 21.2 marks at 239, recovered later after the company denied involvement in allegations of graphite electrode price fixing.
British shares closed at their best levels of the day as continued takeover bid speculation overshadowed the reality of increased British interest rates and the threat of a U.S. fiscal tightening.
The FTSE 100 index, which started the week at 4,621.3, closed at 4,645.0, up 68.8 points on the day but only 23.3 points firmer over the five-day period.

"It's been a good end to a nervy week," the head of trading at a large brokerage said. "We got a rate hike and the U.S. numbers out of the way without a major hiccup. Now all that's left is the (UK) Budget."
Continued hopes for takeover bids countered the Bank of England's decision to push up British interest rates.
"The market had pretty much discounted the hike. The hope how is that by acting early the Bank won't have to put rates up much higher this year," one trader said.
French shares ignored political uncertainty to finish higher for the sixth straight trading day, helped by Wall Street's performance.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed near its intra-session high, finishing up 1.06 percent or 28.40 points at 2,719.25, while the CAC-40 futures contract was up 16 points at 2,707
The CAC-40 index has risen 194 points since Sunday's parliamentary election vaulted the Socialists into power in an alliance with the Communist Party and Greens.
CURRENCIES AT 1615 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7261 marks and 115.23 yen compared with 1.7285 marks and 115.65 yen in late European trading on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS -- CLOSING LEVELS
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index closed up 68.8 points, or 1.5 percent, at 4,645.0.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed up 28.40 points, or 1.06 percent, at 2,719.25.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended up 22.26 points, or 0.61 percent, at 3,695.29. In later screen trade, the IBIS-DAX index ended at 3,700.53.
PRECIOUS METALS
Platinum ended sharply higher at $490.00, while palladium ended at $224.15. Gold finished at $344.45, up $2.70 and silver was nine cents firmer at $4.87.
